plugins.name: code-review
plugins.description: Structured code review and repository audit. Reviews a diff, branch or pull request against correctness, security, performance and accessibility, and reports findings ranked by severity with a concrete failure scenario for each. Use when asked to review code, audit a PR, or check quality before merging.

plugins.name: debugger
plugins.description: Diagnoses failures down to their mechanism before changing any code. Reproduces the fault deterministically, narrows it to the smallest failing case, bisects regressions to the commit that introduced them, and proves the fix with a test that fails without it. Use when something is broken, a test fails or is flaky, behaviour regressed after a change, or a crash, stack trace or incident needs a root cause.

plugins.name: developer
plugins.description: The feature development loop: orient in the code, write a change plan, implement it in verifiable slices, run the repository's own checks, and self-review before handoff. Also covers behaviour-preserving refactors. Use when asked to implement a feature, build or add functionality, work a ticket, refactor existing code, or check that a change is finished.

plugins.name: interview-prep
plugins.description: Prepares an engineer for one specific interview loop, not interviews in general. Maps the rounds a job description implies, ranks what to fix by risk, and runs graded mock rounds -- recruiter screen, live coding, take-home review, system design, behavioral, hiring manager -- against a rubric willing to say no. Keeps the STAR story bank and what real rounds asked. Use when preparing for an interview, practising answers, running a mock, building behavioral stories, or debriefing a round.

plugins.name: job-hunter
plugins.description: Runs a job or contract search as a pipeline instead of a pile of tabs. Scores a posting against a declared profile and says pursue or skip with the reason, writes portfolio case studies from a codebase or live app, tailors the application to one posting, and tracks every opportunity with follow-ups that come due. Use when reviewing a job ad, gig or RFP, deciding whether to apply or bid, writing a proposal, cover letter or CV variant, or asking what needs chasing.

plugins.name: pair-programmer
plugins.description: Pairs on code instead of taking it over. Navigates while you drive -- holding the goal, questioning decisions before they are typed, catching a change spreading past its scope -- or plays TDD ping-pong where the suite decides when a turn ends. Keeps a journal of decisions, rejected alternatives and next steps, so work can be handed over. Use when the user wants to pair, asks for a second pair of eyes while coding, asks for ping-pong or test-first pairing, or asks whether a change is on track.

plugins.name: recruiter-inbox
plugins.description: An actor agent for recruiter conversations on LinkedIn and email. Sweeps LinkedIn messages and InMails in your signed-in Chrome and recruiter email in Gmail, triages each one, drafts the reply that moves it toward a first call, and sends only the text you approved word for word; a hook stops anything else. Tracks who owes whom a reply. Use when answering recruiters, LinkedIn job offer messages, salary questions or follow-ups.

plugins.name: scrum-master
plugins.description: Backlog refinement and sprint planning against GitHub Issues. Turns raw requests into ready stories with acceptance criteria and a size, splits the ones that are too big, and builds a sprint plan with one goal and a capacity number that survives contact with reality. Use when asked to refine or groom a backlog, write a user story, add acceptance criteria, estimate work, or plan the next sprint.
